objective.text: Order a compound index to support the specified equality filter and ordered scan.

difficulty.rationale: Align the leading key with tenant equality and the remaining keys with a deterministic ordered scan.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

assumptions: PostgreSQL 18, B-tree index, query WHERE tenant_id = ? ORDER BY created_at ASC, id ASC LIMIT 50. No other predicates.

stem: Which proposed index order directly supports narrowing to one tenant and scanning that tenant in the requested order, without assuming the planner must choose it?

options.rationale: Equality on the leading tenant key leaves rows ordered by created_at and id within that tenant’s index range.
This leads with time across all tenants, so it does not provide the same contiguous tenant-first range.
options.misconception: This leads with time across all tenants, so it does not provide the same contiguous tenant-first range.

options.rationale: Within the tenant, this orders primarily by id rather than created_at.
options.misconception: Within the tenant, this orders primarily by id rather than created_at.

options.text: Separate indexes on tenant_id and created_at
options.rationale: Independent indexes do not themselves provide the specified composite ordered path including the id tiebreaker.
options.misconception: Independent indexes do not themselves provide the specified composite ordered path including the id tiebreaker.
